title: "Compensation Study"

## Contract

- **Consultant:** Koff & Associates
- **Council approval date:** July 19, 2022
- **Work began:** August 31, 2022
- **Estimated completion (per March 2023 City progress report):** September 2023
- **Actual delivery:** February 2024

::: {.source-note}
Approval and start dates: *El Cerrito CAP Progress Report, March 2023.pdf*, Executive Summary — "The City Council approved a contract with Koff and Associates for a Citywide classification/compensation study on July 19, 2022. Koff and Associates began their work as of August 31, 2022 and the study is slated to be completed in September 2023."
:::

## Methodology Gaps (documented separately, prior research)

- Does not account for CalPERS Unfunded Actuarial Liability (UAL) anywhere in its total-compensation analysis — only prices normal-cost pension add-ons.
- Comparator cities (15 total) averaged approximately 71,500 residents versus El Cerrito's approximately 25,700 — roughly 2.8–2.9 times larger on average.
- The City Manager position was excluded entirely from the benchmark list.
- Found base salary 7.9% below market median, but total compensation only 1.9% below median.
- El Cerrito's 37.5-hour workweek (for Management & Confidential and SEIU 1021 employees) was not adjusted for in the comparator methodology.

::: {.source-note}
These findings are drawn from prior analysis of the Koff study itself (February 2024) and comparator-city data; page-level citations to the Koff report should be added directly from the report document when available for public citation.
:::

## Why Sequencing Matters Here

This study benchmarked El Cerrito's compensation against other cities' compensation for the same positions — without any prior, independent analysis of whether those positions' duties, staffing levels, or organizational structure were appropriately scoped. That structural/duties analysis is exactly what the State Auditor's recommended sequence called for as Step 1 and Step 2, *before* any compensation benchmarking (Step 3). See the [Sequencing Case Study](sequencing-case-study.qmd) for the full comparison.
